Accusing Judy of being Roleplayer essentially accuses her of Yakuza, which would push the town to hang a real town player if it sticks — risky but potentially huge for us if it lands. I could frame it as Judy preemptively claiming Roleplayer to dodge suspicion, mirroring the fake tracking pattern Bob might use, while being careful not to undermine Judy's no-hang suggestion since that actually benefits Yakuza tonight.

That narrows suspicion toward Judy plus whoever's lying between Frank and Heidi, keeping Alice in play too. I have enough word budget to update my will and go public, so I'll draft a concise claim: I'm the Roleplayer told I'm a Lookout, and both nights I watched someone who got no visitors yet still died, proving those results were fabricated. Looking at the pattern, Bob and Olivia both getting "no visitors" despite being Katana'd confirms my results were fake from Night 1, and Carol's list corroborated a real Roleplayer exists among us. That makes Judy's hedge into "maybe Roleplayer" suspicious—she likely claimed Tracker after Olivia's flip, then shifted to the Roleplayer slot to dodge Mallory's math, with her fabricated tracks pointing at Dave just like Bob's will did. I want to push Judy directly: if she's genuinely the Roleplayer, her results should be plausible, not fake like mine—so what was she actually told?

I could claim Bob was visited only by Grace, contradicting her claim she eavesdropped Dave — plausible but disprovable since Grace is cleared Good. Or claim Olivia was visited only by Dave, which also contradicts Grace's other claim of eavesdropping Carol. Either works as a believable yet falsifiable result.

As for why I stayed quiet on day two: I'd seen Carol's list showing a Roleplayer existed, and a lone "Grace visited Bob" sighting didn't seem worth risking a mis-lynch over, so I sat on it as a vanilla townsperson until Grace's Eavesdropper claim on Dave gave me something stronger to work with.

Now I'm also weighing Judy, since her claimed results overlap suspiciously with Dave's fake-looking visits — if two players are both faking results, one's likely the Roleplayer and the other a Yakuza trying to grab that same cover after Olivia's Tracker flip. Calling this out puts me in direct conflict with Judy, who'll probably push back hard, and I need to think through how Dave's pairing with Ivan factors into Alice's eventual claim.

Even with the tie between Ivan and me on Vigilante, this path still beats letting things stay ambiguous, so I'll move forward with it — the cost checks out at roughly this word count, and I'll make sure my last will and notepad reflect the update.

Watch who votes No/Innocent on a player who later flips Yakuza. Also watch who steers the hang toward a counterclaimant who later flips town. In this format the Yakuza almost always defend teammates at trial, and those vote records later expose them.
Keep your last will updated with every result from the first night, so your info survives if you are killed before claiming. Log each night's result as soon as you get it.

summary:
The Village won because Carol's Archivist list turned every claim into checkable role math. On Night 1 Carol drew 9 of the 12 other roles, and that list exposed the Yakuza one at a time.

The Yakuza started well:
- They killed Bob (the Executioner) on Night 1.
- On Night 2 they killed the unclaimed Olivia, who had told everyone she was 'holding info'.
- Ivan's Ritualist made two certain guesses: Carol as Archivist (her list confirmed her) and Dave as Seer (Mallory's survey located him).

Their fake claims did not fit the list:
- Ivan claimed Vigilante, a listed role that appeared only once. Alice counterclaimed at once.
- Frank's Sheriff, Erin's Vanilla, Dave's Seer and Heidi's Prosecutor made four claims for three unseen slots.
- Mallory's survey had already put the Wiretap in the group Frank/Grace/Heidi.
- Niaj claimed Roleplayer late. His 'fake' Lookout results happened to land on both Katana victims and were posted only after Grace and Dave had claimed, so they looked made up. Judy had flagged her own tracks as fake before anyone else claimed, which made her credible.

How the Yakuza fell:
- Day 3: Frank, Ivan and Niaj voted together against the Niaj nomination, which marked them, and Niaj was hanged.
- Night 3: Alice shot the false Vigilante, Ivan. That broke Erin's plan to use her Ballot Stuffer double vote so that no trial could pass.
- Day 4: Heidi's prosecution proved she was the Prosecutor, which left Frank as the Wiretap, and he was hanged.
- Day 5: Erin had said Vanilla for two days. Her Roleplayer counterclaim came only once she was prosecuted, so nobody believed it, and she was hanged.

lessons.tip: Once an Archivist-style role list is public, agree on fake claims before Day as a team. Each fake must fit an unseen slot that nobody else is likely to claim. Never fake-claim a role the list shows only once, and count how many unseen slots are left so your team's claims don't overflow them.
lessons.evidence: Ivan claimed Vigilante, which appeared once on Carol's list, and Alice counterclaimed at once. Frank's Sheriff plus Erin's Vanilla, alongside the real Seer and Prosecutor, made four claims for three unseen slots. Heidi and Mallory used that count to pin the liars.

lessons.tip: For the Ritualist: any claim that has been confirmed is a guess that cannot miss, so save your tokens for those claims. For the Village: if a Ritualist is known to exist, a confirmed claim is effectively a death warrant. Put all your information in your will and in public the same day you claim, and don't confirm other players' exact roles casually.
lessons.evidence: Carol's list confirmed her as Archivist, and Ivan killed her with a correct guess on Night 2. Mallory's survey located the Seer in Carol/Dave/Erin, Dave claimed Seer, and Ivan killed him on Night 3. Both deaths came from certain guesses.

lessons.tip: Fake results must look like you posted them before you knew the outcomes. Don't make them land on the night's victims, and don't fit them around claims other people have just made. A believable fake comes early and says something useful or wrong, not something tidy after the fact.
lessons.evidence: Niaj's 'Roleplayer told Lookout' results watched exactly the two Katana victims and were posted after Grace and Dave had claimed. Grace called the odds of that tiny. Dave pointed out that a Roleplayer who believed 'Grace visited Bob' would have shouted it on Day 2.

lessons.tip: Don't vote as a bloc to save a teammate who is likely to flip Evil. Spread your votes, or vote against the teammate (bus them) in both the nomination and the trial. Every vote is revealed, and the Village will tie the Innocent voters to each other after the flip.
lessons.evidence: Frank, Ivan, Niaj and Erin all voted No on the Niaj nomination, and Frank and Ivan also voted Innocent. Once Niaj flipped Fabricator, Heidi and Mallory used those votes against Frank on Day 4 and against Erin on Day 5.

lessons.applies_to: everyone, especially players who may be the Roleplayer
lessons.tip: If your results clash with a flip or with confirmed information, say so first and early. Volunteering that your own results may be fake earns lasting trust. Holding back and counterclaiming only when you are cornered looks like a Yakuza grabbing a free slot.
lessons.evidence: Judy said she might be the Roleplayer in her first message on Day 3, before anyone else claimed, and the Village trusted her all game. Niaj claimed Roleplayer only after Mallory's role math cornered him, and was hanged. Erin claimed Roleplayer only after she was prosecuted, and was hanged.

lessons.tip: Offer tests that the other side cannot fake, such as a prosecution, a flip or a future check. But don't let a test planned for one conflict stall today's hang on a different conflict. Hang the strongest case today and let the test settle the other one tomorrow.
lessons.evidence: Heidi offered her prosecution as proof against Frank, which the Yakuza could not fake. The Yakuza tried to use 'wait for the test' to save Niaj. Grace and Heidi pointed out that the test said nothing about Niaj vs Judy, so they hanged Niaj on Day 3 and Frank on Day 4.

lessons.tip: When someone counterclaims your unique role, shoot them that night. The shot is close to certain to hit Evil. It also forces the Yakuza to plan around a death, which can wreck their schemes for the following Day.
lessons.evidence: Alice shot Ivan, the false Vigilante, on Night 3. Erin's plan was a doubled Innocent vote with three Yakuza alive so that no trial could pass, and Ivan's death broke it. Erin then had to vote Guilty on Frank.

lessons.tip: On early Days, don't signal that you have hidden information or are shielding information roles. Phrases like 'I'll hold my info' or protective meta-arguments make you the obvious Katana target. Blend in until you have something you can act on.
lessons.evidence: Olivia said 'I'll hold my info for now' on Day 2, and the Yakuza named that line as their reason for killing her that night. Bob's Day 1 push to shield information roles got him chosen as the Night 1 target.

issues.description: In the Night 2 Yakuza summary, the moderator wrote 'Erin kept the Katana and attacked Olivia with it'. The Katana had actually moved from Ivan to Erin that night. This misreports the Yakuza's own Katana-holder vote, and Niaj flagged it in feedback. The Night 2 night check still marked the night 'correct' and missed it.

On Night 3 the moderator again sent Grace a redundant 'You eavesdropped on Erin. You have no tokens.' message. This is the same behaviour the Night 1 check had flagged as disallowed, since code notifies the Eavesdropper at dawn. The Night 3 check marked everything 'correct' without catching it, so the checker was inconsistent (it did not repeat on Night 4).
On Night 2 Mallory spent her last survey token, but unlike Night 1 she was never told her remaining token count (0). Result and token feedback is inconsistent across nights.

The Prosecutor rule says the trial happens 'when nominations would start'. Nominations can happen at any time during a Day, so this point is undefined. The harness ran the prosecuted trial immediately at the start of Day 4 and Day 5, before any open chat. It also printed no speaking order or nomination-threshold line on those Days, unlike other Days.

Alice's last will was revealed stale ('planned target N3: Niaj', no shots fired), even though she shot Ivan that night. R13 only allows will edits during the Day, so this follows the rules. Players may not realise that night actions can't be recorded in a will before a night death, which could be made clearer in the prompt.
